title: External processors: trust
goal: Assess an external processor’s source and prepare safe verification without running unknown code.
prerequisites: 1c-enterprise.a 6; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.
outcomes: Assess an external processor’s source and prepare safe verification without running unknown code.
Complete a teaching file’s provenance record.
Compare two copies after a comment change.
sections: An external processor can read/change data, access files and use available platform actions. Its extension does not make it safe; nor does a familiar sender prove unchanged content. Establish author, purpose, official source and required rights before opening anything. Never execute an unknown file out of curiosity.

Start reports from a testable question, not a layout. Name period, customer, status, resource and units, then list expected document identities. Sum, row count and group count answer different questions. Without this distinction, a plausible setting can answer the wrong question. A small independent table lets reviewers identify the first mismatch rather than guessing from appearance.
A hash binds review to a file

SHA256 binds a reviewed copy to later bytes; it does not itself prove harmlessness. A malicious file also has a hash. Compare against a trusted channel and attach review to that exact copy. Any modification creates new bytes requiring a new review.

Saved variants preserve available settings, not necessarily a frozen dataset. New documents can change results. Archive parameters, time, membership and observed totals separately. Reopen the variant itself:a familiar title can remain after a required filter was lost or experimentally changed. Compare actual settings rather than trusting names or save notifications.
An infobase copy does not isolate the computer

A copy protects source records from ordinary mistakes but does not confine code to that directory. A test infobase is not permission to run unknownBSL on the main computer. Safe mode and rights have specific contexts; full execution isolation requires an agreed boundary and evidence, not a checkbox.

Distinguish settings from executing a program component. External processors can modify data and act outside an infobase; an infobase copy is not host isolation. Decline execution from unknown sources and request provenance review. Hashes prove equal bytes; security needs authority analysis and a verified execution boundary appropriate to the scenario.

Without a trusted source and approved environment, the outcome isNOTRUN with a reason and specialist request. That is a correct decision, not a learning failure. Practice with original teaching source and predicted actions. Execute only after admission, on synthetic data, with before/after state checks and bounded output.

End consulting with reproducible explanation. Parameter discrepancies need setting corrections; missing fields/algorithms need a development request. Share expected/actual, steps and tested causes without secrets or real infobases. Repeat the workflow after changes. A closed ticket is not acceptance and does not turn untested permissions or exports intoPASS.
